LESSON: A refusal rule written as a SUBSTRING match eventually refuses the thing that was right. `data-tile` matched `data-tile-sized` and the twelve-tile-grid guard fired on the design's own artwork; `Compose` matched `composes`. Split forbidden WORDS (exact, word-boundary) from forbidden TOKENS (substring) and carry the kind in the data, not in a regex a later editor can flatten.

A GUARD WRITTEN AS A BICONDITIONAL CAN NEVER REPORT THE DEFECT IT EXISTS FOR. Checking that `None on file` is outside the vocabulary AND that the fact is recorded made finding the defect abort the instrument (exit 2) instead of reporting it (exit 1). A premise guard must be one-directional: assert the FACT, then let the finding flow through as a finding.

SCOPE MUST BE STRUCTURAL, NOT CONVENTIONAL. Every read scoped to an explicit `<main data-lens-body="…">` marker, with a no-marker board ABORTING rather than falling back to the whole document. Otherwise chrome (nav badges, top-bar badges) silently satisfies or violates rules about the body — this lane's own nav-badge rule and fixture-badge rule were both wrong in opposite directions before the scope was made total.

A VACUOUS PREDICATE NEEDS ITS OWN RULE ID (R13), not a silent pass and not a generic abort. 'This board gave that rule no input' and 'this board broke that rule' are different statements, and an exit code alone cannot tell them apart. Real boards are often the only source of a count, so breaking one to plant a defect removes the inputs the OTHER rules need — plant into a COPY instead.

TWO FILES ASSERTING THE SAME FACT NEED A READ THAT JOINS THEM. canvas.json and source-state.json both named a product commit with nothing comparing them; `checkCommitTie` now aborts on a mismatch and the mismatch is planted.

THE DISPATCH'S PREDICTED END-STATE IS NOT EVIDENCE. This dispatch asked for 'R4 down to one finding (work:records)'. A live sibling lane moved that line in the same window and R4 went to zero. Report what the instrument says.

Do NOT plant a violation by editing a real artboard in place.
